name: application-world-clock-row
title: World Clock Row
description: List of timezone rows showing city, UTC offset, current time, and a sun/moon icon indicating day or night in that location.
useWhen: Distributed teams need to see teammates' or offices' current local time at a glance.
Scheduling across timezones benefits from a quick day/night visual cue before picking a meeting time.
You want a compact list rather than a full calendar or scheduling grid.
avoidWhen: Only a single timezone is relevant — a plain timestamp is simpler than a list.
You need to pick a meeting time across zones, not just view current times — pair this with a scheduling component instead of using it alone.
Precision to the second matters — this is a glanceable display, not a live-ticking clock; add your own interval-based update if seconds precision is required.
responsiveBehavior: The list is a fixed max-w-sm block that fills its container's available width up to that cap at all breakpoints.
accessibility: The sun/moon icon is aria-hidden since day/night state is supplementary to the always-visible time and offset text.
Times are rendered in a monospace font for alignment, but remain plain text readable by screen readers in natural reading order.
Each row groups city, offset, and time together so screen reader users hear them as one unit.

variants.title: World clock row
variants.description: Four-city timezone list with UTC offsets, current times, and sun/moon day-night icons.
accessibility: Day/night is also implied by the visible time and offset, so the icon is a reinforcing cue, not the only signal.

variants.title: World clock row (Dark)
variants.description: World clock row adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Icon and text colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
